tool-cloakbrowser.title: CloakBrowser: a Chromium drop-in for Playwright with C++-level fingerprint patches
tool-cloakbrowser.note: A custom Chromium build that drops straight into Playwright, 87 C++-level patches, with humanize and proxy support. Wrapper code is MIT, the binary needs a license key.

sections.t: Use responsibly: this is a browser that spoofs device identity for automation. Only use it on your own sites, on public data you're allowed to collect, or with permission. Automation that breaks terms of service (especially on Facebook, Zalo, TikTok...) can get accounts banned and may be illegal. CloakBrowser's README also explicitly forbids unauthorized automation, credential stuffing and abusive account creation.

Info taken from the repo's GitHub page, read on 4/11/2026. Stars, versions and terms may have changed, and the claims about passing bot checks come from the author; I haven't verified them independently.
Quick comparison with Camoufox

head: Criteria
CloakBrowser
Camoufox
rows: MIT wrapper, binary needs a license key
Free tier limited to one concurrent session, Pro plan available
Linux, Windows, macOS, doesn't run on WSL
Under development, may not be stable for production

sections.t: My take: if you need Chromium, want a supported prebuilt binary and are fine with a license key, look at CloakBrowser. If you need fully open source with no key, and can accept the Firefox engine and the 'not stable for production' note, look at Camoufox. Either way, test it on your own use case.
Repo info

head: Item
Details
rows: A custom Chromium build, a drop-in replacement for Playwright (Puppeteer supported)
Linux x86_64 and arm64, macOS arm64 and x86_64, Windows x86_64
About 32.7k stars, 2.7k forks, 137 open issues, 390 commits
Wrapper code (Python, JS, .NET): MIT. Chromium binary: separate license, needs a license key
README says 'Last tested: Nov 2026' and describes itself as maintained

sections.t: Highlights

items: Fingerprints are patched in Chromium's C++ source, not via JavaScript injection or config flags. The binary's Ed25519 signature is verified before extraction.
humanize=True: Bézier-curve mouse movement, typing with random delays, natural-paced scrolling.
HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy support, geoip=True to match timezone and language to the proxy IP, WebRTC IP spoofing.
Persistent profiles (keeps cookies and localStorage between runs) and Chrome extension loading.
Poses as Windows by default on Linux and Windows, with an optional macOS identity.
cloakserve runs the browser as a CDP server; there's a Docker image, a .NET client and a CLI (install binary, diagnostics, cache management).

sections.t: Installation

pip install cloakbrowser

npm install cloakbrowser playwright-core   # or puppeteer-core

dotnet add package CloakBrowser

items: The ~200 MB binary downloads automatically on first run and is cached. No need to run playwright install chromium, but you still need the system libraries Playwright requires.
launch() returns a Playwright Browser object, so new_page(), close()... work as usual. Switching from Playwright only means changing the browser launch code.

sections.t: License and license key (important)

head: Plan
Terms
rows: Sign up with email to get a key, one concurrent session. Always gets the latest build
More concurrent sessions, can pin a Chromium version to roll back
Personal and commercial per the README, no redistributing the binary. Serving third parties needs an OEM or SaaS license

items: Every launch needs the key, set via the CLOAKBROWSER_LICENSE_KEY environment variable. Don't put the key in source code or chats.
The keyless v146 binary is only in the old wrapper (pip install "cloakbrowser<0.7") and no longer gets updates.
Full terms are in the repo's BINARY-LICENSE.md; read it before commercial use.

sections.t: Limitations the README admits

items: It doesn't solve CAPTCHAs, it tries to keep them from appearing. No built-in proxy rotation; you bring your own proxies.
Some sites still detect headless mode; running headed is recommended (use Xvfb on Linux).
On Linux, a convincing Windows identity needs real Windows fonts installed, and a macOS identity needs real Mac fonts.
Puppeteer can be detected by reCAPTCHA Enterprise, so Playwright is recommended. page.wait_for_timeout() and page.evaluate() may send CDP commands some systems can spot.
Playwright's context.request and route.fetch() don't go through SOCKS5 or authenticated proxies.
The README admits detection may catch up in the future; it's an ongoing arms race.

sections.t: Ideas for using it in the Library

items: Test your own website and landing pages across many browser setups and regions.
Run browser agents on a VPS (pairs with the OVH VPS for Hermes Agent guide) to get blocked by mistake less often when accessing public data you're allowed to use.
Study how anti-bot systems work, in your own environment.

sections.t: Install safety notes

items: There are many forks and look-alikes (such as zapabob, DivMode, dgtlmoon, Munasco) with different numbers. Only use the official CloakHQ/CloakBrowser repo and the author's own PyPI or npm packages.
The prebuilt binary is downloaded from the publisher, so run it in an isolated environment (a separate VPS or Docker), away from API keys, passwords or important data.

sections.t: Link

tool-camoufox.title: Camoufox: open-source anti-detect Firefox for scraping and AI agents
tool-camoufox.note: A Firefox build that spoofs fingerprints, driven by Playwright, with humanize, geoip and proxy. Browser MPL-2.0, packages MIT. Under development.

sections.t: Use responsibly: this is a browser that spoofs device identity for automation. Only use it on your own sites, on public data you're allowed to collect, or with permission. Automation that breaks terms of service (especially on Facebook, Zalo, TikTok...) can get accounts banned and may be illegal. CloakBrowser's README also explicitly forbids unauthorized automation, credential stuffing and abusive account creation.

Info taken from the repo's GitHub page, read on 4/11/2026. Stars, versions and terms may have changed, and the claims about passing bot checks come from the author; I haven't verified them independently.
Repo info

head: Item
Details
rows: An open-source anti-detect Firefox build for web scraping and AI agents, driven by Playwright
Playwright uses Firefox's built-in Juggler protocol; automation code runs in an isolated world the page can't see
About 13.0k stars, 1.1k forks, 38 open issues, 14 pull requests, 916 commits
Browser (patches and build): MPL-2.0. Python and TypeScript packages: MIT. Cursory mouse data: LGPLv3 or later
camoufox.com and the READMEs in the repo (python, typescript, docs)
README says: 'This project is under development. It may not be suitable for stable production use.'

sections.t: Highlights

items: Each launch gets a consistent device identity, generated from real-world device distributions.
Fingerprint spoofing: navigator, screen, WebGL, WebGPU, fonts, audio, voices, media devices, timezone, locale, geolocation, WebRTC IP.
humanize=True: human-like mouse movement, based on recordings of real interactions.
Multiple identities in one browser via NewContext().
Ships with uBlock Origin, with telemetry and unneeded extras stripped out.

sections.t: Install and use

pip install -U "camoufox[geoip]"
camoufox fetch

npm install camoufox playwright-core
npx camoufox fetch

from camoufox.sync_api import Camoufox

with Camoufox(headless=True) as browser:
    page = browser.new_page()
    # use it like regular Playwright
The returned browser is a standard Playwright Browser. In Node.js use const browser = await Camoufox({ headless: true }).
Main options

head: Option
What it does
rows: True, or the max seconds per mouse movement
proxy with geoip=True so timezone, language, location and WebRTC IP match the exit IP
True, or 'virtual' and 'virtual-gpu' (the last two on Linux only)
Set the OS per context via NewContext(browser, os=...)
Turn canvas noise on or off
fingerprint_preset, locale, addons, exclude_addons, pin_cpu_cores, main_world_eval, launch_server()

sections.t: The full list is in the repo's python/README.md.
Operating systems

items: Builds run on Linux; Windows and macOS versions are cross-compiled. Packaged architectures: x86_64, arm64, and i686 (Windows only).
The README states 'WSL does not work', so it can't run on WSL.
WebGPU is only available on Windows and Apple-silicon Macs.

sections.t: Limitations the README admits

items: Camoufox only spoofs Firefox identities. Some systems check SpiderMonkey-specific behavior, so it can't pass as Chromium.
Canvas on an OS different from the real machine returns random data and can give it away. Audio rendering and text width results aren't noised.
Enabling instantAnimations can get the browser detected. Media codecs on Linux depend on the libraries installed on the machine.
The README admits Camoufox can still be detected.

sections.t: Maintenance status to watch

items: One fork says the original maintainer has had health issues since 3/2025. That's from a fork and I haven't verified it; check the original repo's commit and issue history to judge how active it is.
Forks list different base Firefox versions (one says 142, another 146); I haven't confirmed which is the latest in the original repo.
The README has a lot of sponsored ads from proxy and scraping service providers, unrelated to what the project does.

sections.t: Install safety notes

items: There are lots of forks named camoufox. Only install from the original daijro/camoufox repo or the official packages, and check the author before installing from a fork.
Run it in an isolated environment (a separate VPS or Docker), away from API keys, passwords or important data.

edit-dji-dlogm-rec709.title: DJI Osmo Pocket 3: LUT D-Log M sang Rec.709
edit-dji-dlogm-rec709.note: DJI's LUT that converts Osmo Pocket 3 D-Log M footage to Rec.709 for color grading in the edit. Description based on the page title and secondary sources.

cta.title: DJI · D-Log M to Rec.709 (Osmo Pocket 3)

sections.t: I couldn't open DJI's download page (the domain was blocked), so I haven't seen the file name, version or instructions there. What follows is based on the page title (D-Log M to Rec.709 for Osmo Pocket 3) and articles I found on the web. The specific steps come from secondary sources, so compare them with DJI's page.
What this download is for

Osmo Pocket 3 can shoot in D-Log M mode: a flat, washed-out image that keeps more highlight and shadow detail for grading. That footage needs converting to a normal color standard to view. The file on DJI's page is a LUT that converts D-Log M to Rec.709, the color space for regular screens. Going by the page title, it's a file for the editing stage, after shooting.
Where it sits in the Edit library
It's in the Editing group because the file is used in editing software. It assumes you shot in D-Log M. If you shot in a normal color mode, you don't need this LUT.
How to use it (from secondary sources, not checked on DJI's page)

head: Software
Steps
rows: Per DJI's LUT guide (a 2018 version written for Resolve 15 and older cameras): copy the file into Color Management's LUT folder, in a DJI subfolder, then click Update Lists (only needed once). Then on the Color page, apply the LUT from the clip's LUT menu. Ctrl+D (Windows) or Command+D (Mac) toggles the before/after comparison
From a third-party tutorial: load the LUT in Lumetri Color, under Basic Correction, Input LUT, then fine-tune with curves and color wheels. This is a secondary source; the menu path isn't confirmed

items: A common Resolve approach: put the DJI LUT on the last node, with other grading nodes before it.
One article notes Premiere Pro sometimes has issues with DJI files, so test a short clip before editing the whole project.

sections.t: A LUT vendor argues DJI's Rec.709 LUT forces footage into Rec.709, so you may lose contrast and blow out highlights. That's the seller's marketing, not independent testing. For deeper grading you can try other LUTs or grade by hand.
To do before using it

skill-brainstorm.title: brainstorm: clarify the problem before you start
skill-brainstorm.note: Interviews you one question at a time to frame the problem as a 6-section brief, deliberately with no solution. Author: Hưng Kescy.

sections.t: Use it when the problem is still fuzzy and you don't want to jump into doing yet. Triggers: brainstorm, thảo luận, làm rõ đề bài (discuss, clarify the brief).
What the skill does

Claude interviews you one question at a time about any kind of work (ops, business, content, code), frames it into a 6-section brief, then has an independent subagent review it for gaps until nothing is left to ask.
3 fixed rules

items: Talk only about the problem, no solutions.
One question per turn, with Claude's recommended answer for you to accept or edit.
Never quietly fill in blanks for you.

sections.t: Step by step

items.d: State the problem in a sentence or two.
Claude reads related docs and folders before asking.
Answer each question. If you don't know, say so.
Claude tells you when it's enough.
A subagent reads the brief and asks more, repeating until it returns NO GAPS.
It's only locked in once you explicitly agree.
The brief is written to docs/briefs/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{slug}.md.

sections.t: /brainstorm I want more sign-ups for my course but I'm not sure where to focus
The brief has 6 sections

head: Section
Content
rows: What exists and how it runs now
What result counts as good enough
At least 3 things deliberately out of scope

sections.t: What you get from the skill
The results below are the outputs the skill itself defines (per its SKILL.md), not measurements from real projects. When you use it and get real results, note them down so they can be added here.

items: One brief file as the single starting point for planning.
The problem is written as a problem, not mixed with solutions, so you don't lock into one direction too early.
Assumptions and unclear points surface before you spend effort on execution.

skill-kf-plan.title: kf-plan: plans that get verified
skill-kf-plan.note: Turns a brief into a plan via a problem tree, prioritization, assumptions and an independent review loop. Version 1.0.1, author Hưng Kescy.

sections.t: Use it after brainstorm, once the problem is clear. Triggers: lên kế hoạch, plan giúp tôi, cập nhật plan (make a plan, plan this for me, update the plan). The skill only plans; it doesn't execute.
Principles

items: Ask in decision groups, each with a recommendation.
You saying 'up to you' doesn't mean Claude can make up facts.
Evidence over memory.
UI features are assumptions that need verifying too.
Good enough beats long.

sections.t: 8 steps

items.d: Read the brief or the framed problem.
What's known, what can be analyzed, what must be probed.
Split the problem into branches.
A 2x2 matrix: impact and controllability.
Each assumption is marked VERIFIED or TO-TEST.
With a separate probe plan for the must-probe items.
A fresh subagent reads it, checks feasibility and failure scenarios, repeating until SUFFICIENT, up to 3 rounds.
Saved only once you explicitly agree.

sections.t: Re-plan mode: when things change, update the old plan and log the changes by date.
/kf-plan docs/briefs/2026-10-28-tang-dang-ky.md
Output: docs/plans/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{slug}.md, built from the assets/plan-template.md template.
What you get from the skill

items: A plan file you can hand to someone else to follow.

The plan has been independently reviewed and checked for failure scenarios before work starts.
Uncertain items go into a probe plan instead of pretending to be certain.

res-tro-ly-24-365.title: Build a 24/365 assistant for working people
res-tro-ly-24-365.note: 7 steps to build a self-running bot for the repetitive tasks of every day, with a case study of the Zalo bot I actually built.
intro: This guide goes from "tasks you repeat every day" to a bot that runs on its own 24/365: it listens on the channel you use daily, understands intent, remembers your own data and does the work for you, even when your computer is off.
I've included a case study of the Zalo and Telegram bot I built (Nomad Lanhmar) to show it really works, plus 10 prompts so you can do it yourself. No coding needed.

outline.d: A workday gets chopped up by follow-up messages, slipping schedules and tasks, forgotten expenses, scattered documents.
Listen, Understand, Remember, Act: only with all 4 blocks is it a real assistant.
Pick the task, pick the channel, the brain, the data, the mode, run 24/365, operate it.
Schedule reminders, text "cà phê 45k" (coffee 45k) and it's logged, turn meeting notes into tasks, search Drive and answer with sources.
How much it costs per month and what I learned from the 6 times the bot tripped up.
A checklist before going live and a prompt set so you can build your own.
